title: Exact solution of the Glauber-Ising model on the finite-length semi-open chain
abstract: The exact time-space correlation function of the $1D$ Glauber-Ising model, quenched to temperature $T=0$ and on a semi-open lattice of finite size $N$, is obtained. This also allows to deduce the exact empty-interval probability of the dual $1D$ coagulation-diffusion process on a periodic finite ring and to reproduce the long-time decay of the particle concentration. These results are consistent with the generic expectations of dynamical finite-size scaling theory.
summary: This paper derives the exact time-space correlation function for the 1D Glauber-Ising model on a semi-open chain at zero temperature. By solving the governing diffusion equation with appropriate boundary conditions, it establishes finite-size scaling functions that connect the magnetic dynamics to the empty-interval probability of a dual coagulation-diffusion process.
main_problem: The primary goal is obtaining the exact time-space correlation function for the 1D Glauber-Ising model on a finite semi-open chain, which also allows deducing properties of the dual coagulation-diffusion process.
main_result: The authors derive explicit finite-size scaling functions for both periodic and semi-open chains, establishing a correspondence between the correlation function and the empty-interval probability for the dual process.
method: The analysis involves solving the equation of motion (a diffusion equation) governing the correlators using Fourier series representations and applying boundary conditions specific to the semi-open geometry.
model_or_system: The system is the 1D Glauber-Ising model, defined on a finite chain segment with spin variables $\sigma_n = \pm 1$. The dynamics are non-equilibrium (Glauber rule) and studied at zero temperature ($T=0$).
key_observables: Time-space correlation function $C(t; r)$, single-time correlator $C_n(t)$, empty-interval probability $E(t, x)$, and particle concentration decay $c(t)$.
important_parameters: Finite size $N$, time $t$, and the ratio of length scale to system size ($N/\sqrt{t}$). The analysis focuses on the $T=0$ limit.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on extending known results for periodic chains to semi-open boundaries, and approximations are noted when simple scaling ansatze fail near crossover regimes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the setup for the semi-open chain calculation. Figure 2 compares the exact semi-open correlator against a simplified scaling ansatz. Figure 3 tests a conjectured mathematical identity relating these two forms.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews results for the periodic ring case, then focuses on extending the methods to the semi-open chain geometry. Finally, it relates these findings to the dual coagulation-diffusion process and derives expressions for particle concentration $c(t)$ using mathematical identities involving theta functions.
why_interesting: This work provides an exact analytical treatment of finite-size effects in non-equilibrium dynamics, which is crucial for understanding crossover phenomena in many physical systems modeled by interacting particles or spin chains.
